title: Foods to Limit or Cook Thoroughly During Pregnancy
excerpt: Food-safety guidance inspired by CDC/NHS/FDA themes: deli meats, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, choosing safe and healthy foods is crucial to ensure the well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we will provide information on foods that pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly to avoid health risks.

## Foods to Limit
According to the CDC, NHS, and FDA, there are certain foods that pregnant women should limit or avoid altogether, including:
* Deli meats and hot dogs: These foods can contain Listeria bacteria, which can harm the fetus.
* Unpasteurized dairy products: Unpasteurized dairy products can contain bacteria like E. coli, Salmonella, and Listeria.
* High-mercury fish: Fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel can contain mercury, which can harm fetal development.
* Undercooked or raw foods: Undercooked or raw foods like sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs can contain bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli.

## Foods to Cook Thoroughly
To ensure safety, pregnant women should cook the following foods thoroughly:
* Meat and poultry: Cook meat and poultry to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to avoid Salmonella and E. coli bacteria.
* Eggs: Cook eggs to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to avoid Salmonella bacteria.
* Seafood: Cook seafood to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C) to avoid Vibrio vulnificus bacteria.

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips to help pregnant women choose safe foods:
* Always check food labels to ensure that they have been pasteurized or cooked thoroughly.
* Avoid eating processed or pre-cooked foods.
* Cook foods at home to ensure that they have been cooked thoroughly.
* Consider using a [meal planner](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner) to get safe and healthy meal ideas.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about food safety, they should seek help from their doctor or a registered dietitian. They can provide specific information and advice to help pregnant women choose safe and healthy foods.

faqs.question: Are deli meats safe for pregnant women?

faqs.question: Can high-mercury fish affect fetal development?
faqs.answer: Yes, high-mercury fish can harm fetal development. Pregnant women should limit or avoid high-mercury fish altogether.
